## Task and progress
**Task:** Compare the model organisms in /research/ on lifespan and experimental throughput. Read every review document, record one finding per organism with `record_finding`, then write a short comparative synthesis.

**Documents found (6) and read status:**
- All six were read in full: celegans_review.md, drosophila_review.md, yeast_review.md, killifish_review.md, mouse_review.md, zebrafish_review.md.
- None remain unread.
- **No findings have been recorded yet.** All six `record_finding` calls are still to do.
- The comparative synthesis has not been written.

## Headline lifespan figures (each document's "Headline" line, standard lab conditions)
| Organism | Median lifespan | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| C. elegans | 18 | days |
| D. melanogaster | 60 | days |
| S. cerevisiae | 25 | divisions (replicative, not time) |
| N. furzeri (killifish) | 16 | weeks |
| M. musculus | 30 | months |
| D. rerio (zebrafish) | 42 | months |

Converted to a common time scale, the order from shortest to longest is:
- C. elegans, about 18 days.
- D. melanogaster, about 60 days.
- Killifish, about 112 days.
- Mouse, about 900 days.
- Zebrafish, about 1,260 days.
- Yeast cannot be converted from divisions to time without a doubling time, which the documents do not give.

I have not derived these conversions in a recorded finding, so treat them as my own arithmetic.

## "Discussion" sections (cohort-level data)
- Each document has a very long Discussion section. It lists several hundred cohort entries in the form: "In cohort X-NN, median survival of <organism> was P% of controls (n=…, <intervention>, lab …)".
- I did not reproduce or aggregate these entries.
- **Interventions:** dietary restriction, heat stress, metformin, rapamycin, daf-2 RNAi.
- **Ranges:**
  - P runs from about 40% to 160%.
  - n runs from about 20 to 400.
  - Labs are numbered 1–40.
- **Pattern:**
  - The entries look noisy and show no consistent direction by intervention or organism.
  - The same intervention gives both much shorter and much longer survival in the same organism.
  - daf-2 RNAi and the other interventions are applied uniformly to every organism, including yeast and zebrafish, which is biologically odd.
  - Cohort IDs repeat with different values. For example, C. elegans cohort H-59 appears several times with different results.
- **Caveat:** I would not draw intervention-effect conclusions from these entries without aggregation, and even then they look unreliable.
- **Throughput:** none of the documents gives explicit throughput numbers, such as animals per experiment, cost, or time per assay. Any throughput comparison has to be inferred from lifespan, so it should be labelled as inference.

2. Write a short comparative synthesis covering:

   - Throughput inferred from lifespan, with the caveat that the documents give no direct throughput data.
   - The data-quality caveats above: noisy cohort entries, repeated cohort IDs, and duplicate provenance numbers (mouse cage bank #118 appears twice; yeast plate lot #547 appears twice).
